column1: narrative
During climb the engine quit after fuel sumps were frozen in winter operations.
Hydraulic leak observed in landing gear during taxi with cold weather.
Water in the fuel system reported after overnight frost and incomplete draining.
Communication breakdown between crew and maintenance delayed troubleshooting of electrical failure.
Seasonal icing contributed to sensor malfunction and subsequent go-around.
On final approach the captain noted an intermittent left main-gear unsafe indication
column2: a go-around was executed and the gear indicated down on the second approach.

column1: During cruise at FL350 the cabin altitude warning illuminated briefly after a pressurization controller hiccup
column2: the crew donned oxygen and descended per QRH.

column1: After pushback the first officer observed a strong odor of Jet-A
column2: ground crew found a fuel truck overflow near the right wing with no ignition source.

column1: While holding for weather the aircraft encountered moderate mixed icing
column2: boots were cycled and the approach was delayed until ice accretion slowed.

column1: A maintenance ferry flight departed with an MEL for an inoperative APU
column2: after shutdown at the destination the APU would not start for gate power.

column1: During taxi the nosewheel steering became intermittent; the crew stopped, coordinated with ATC, and requested a tow after confirming hydraulic quantity normal.
Climbing through 10,000 ft the crew received a traffic alert for a VFR aircraft that had not been pointed out by departure; TCAS resolution was not required.
After landing the thrust reverser on the right engine unlocked late
column2: reverse thrust was cancelled and braking used to clear the runway.

column1: Overnight overnight battery charge was incomplete
column2: on first engine start the GPU was required and the logbook showed prior deferred charging issues.

column1: A contract mechanic reported a cracked engine mount bolt during a scheduled inspection
column2: the aircraft was grounded pending replacement.

column1: During a night visual approach the runway lights appeared dimmer than expected
column2: after landing the airport reported a partial lighting circuit failure.

column1: The FO mis-set the altimeter by 1 in Hg after leaving high terrain
column2: the error was caught in the approach briefing before descent.

column1: Cabin crew reported a passenger oxygen mask dangling after takeoff
column2: the panel was reset and maintenance deferred inspection at the next station.

column1: A bird strike on climbout produced a vibration in the #2 engine
column2: thrust was reduced and the flight returned with emergency equipment standing by.

column1: Dispatch released the flight with a known MEL for an inoperative fuel quantity indicator
column2: the crew cross-checked totalizer and dipstick readings before departure.

column1: During deicing the Type IV fluid application was interrupted by radio congestion
column2: the crew asked for a reapplication before takeoff.

column1: An ATC frequency change was missed during a busy SID
column2: the crew queried the previous frequency and re-established contact within two minutes.

column1: A cargo handler reported smoke odor near a lithium battery shipment
column2: the pallet was removed before loading and the fire department inspected.

column1: On a ferry flight with flaps restricted by MEL the approach was flown at higher speed
column2: landing distance was recalculated and accepted.

column1: The captain declined an intersection takeoff after reviewing wet-runway performance charts that left insufficient margin.
During cruise a generator failed offline
column2: the crew followed the electrical abnormal checklist and diverted to the nearest suitable airport.

column1: A student pilot in the traffic pattern cut off a departing aircraft on the upwind
column2: the tower issued go-around instructions to both.

column1: Hydraulic system B quantity dropped during flap extension
column2: flaps were retracted to the previous setting and an emergency was declared.

column1: The FO's headset failed mid-flight
column2: the crew used the hand mic and spare headset from the jumpseat bag.

column1: After a hard landing inspection revealed a tire flat spot
column2: the tire was replaced before the next revenue leg.

column1: A NOTAM for temporary crane activity near the approach path was missed in the briefing package
column2: ATC provided traffic advisories.

column1: Cabin temperature control stuck in full cold
column2: several passengers complained and the packs were manually managed for the remainder of the flight.

column1: A fuel imbalance developed after a valve misconfiguration during crossfeed training on a simulator session that mirrored a prior line event.
The aircraft returned to the gate after a takeoff warning horn sounded with flaps set correctly
column2: a sensor fault was later confirmed.

column1: During pushback the tug driver reported a brake fire smell
column2: engines were shut down and ARFF responded

column1: An RNAV approach became unstable below 1,000 ft AGL due to a late runway change; a missed approach was flown.
Maintenance deferred a cracked windshield outer ply under the MEL
column2: the crew briefed reduced visibility procedures for night arrival.

column1: A jumpseat rider noted that the oxygen pressure gauge was below redline before departure
column2: the bottle was replaced.

column1: Wake turbulence from a heavy departure caused a momentary uncommanded roll on climb
column2: the autopilot was disconnected and the aircraft was re-trimmed.

column1: The crew received a TCAS RA climbing through a busy terminal area
column2: both aircraft responded and separation was restored.

column1: A runway incursion occurred when a vehicle crossed without clearance during low visibility taxi
column2: the departing crew rejected takeoff at low speed.

column1: Electrical odor in the galley led cabin crew to pull circuit breakers for the coffee makers
column2: maintenance found a shorted heating element.

column1: An intermittent stick-shaker on approach in icing conditions led to a go-around
column2: boots and anti-ice were confirmed on for the second approach.

column1: The FO entered an incorrect FMC departure runway
column2: the error was caught during the before-takeoff checklist when the runway disagreed with the ATIS.

column1: A cargo smoke warning activated in cruise; the checklist was completed, no smoke was observed, and the flight continued after coordination with dispatch and ATC.
During a night cargo operation the crew noted an unlatched cargo door light after rotation
column2: they returned and found the sensor misrigged.

column1: A controller issued a descent clearance through an occupied altitude
column2: the crew queried and held level until traffic was clear.

column1: Oil pressure on the left engine trended down over two hours
column2: the QRH led to a precautionary shutdown and diversion.

column1: After landing the spoilers failed to deploy automatically
column2: manual spoiler extension and aggressive braking stopped the aircraft on the remaining runway.

column1: A first-cycle captain under supervision mis-briefed the missed approach
column2: the check airman intervened before the approach was begun.

column1: Ground icing was present but Type I only was applied
column2: the crew refused takeoff until Type IV was applied per company cold-weather procedures.

column1: An altitude bust of 400 ft occurred after an early level-off call was blocked on frequency
column2: TCAS did not alert and ATC issued a turn.

column1: The APU fire bottle squib tested failed during preflight
column2: maintenance replaced the bottle and the departure was delayed 90 minutes.

column1: A passenger medical emergency required diversion
column2: medical personnel met the aircraft and oxygen was administered in flight.

column1: The crew noted conflicting TCAS targets that did not match ATC traffic calls
column2: they requested verification and adjusted heading.

column1: During a visual approach the landing gear would not extend electrically
column2: alternate extension was used and the landing was uneventful.

column1: A fuel truck parked under the wing with the beacon off
column2: the FO refused boarding until the truck repositioned clear of the engines.

column1: An MEL for an inoperative anti-skid channel required higher landing speeds
column2: the crew selected a longer runway.

column1: Cabin crew reported a burning smell near seat-row electrical outlets
column2: the affected circuit was isolated and maintenance met the flight.

column1: A late weight-and-balance revision reduced takeoff thrust margin
column2: the captain elected a full-length runway and max thrust.

column1: The autopilot disconnected repeatedly in moderate turbulence
column2: the crew flew manually and requested a lower altitude.

column1: A maintenance write-up for recurring pack overheat was closed without finding root cause
column2: the pack tripped again on the next flight.

column1: During an RNAV missed approach the published climb gradient could not be met with one engine inop practice thrust
column2: a different missed procedure was briefed.

column1: The crew observed a drone near the final approach path and broke off the approach
column2: ATC was notified and the airport temporarily closed the runway.

column1: A check airman noted that the FO's scan broke down during a raw-data ILS
column2: the maneuver was discontinued for training debrief.

column1: Hydraulic fluid was found pooled under the belly after overnight parking
column2: a leaking fitting was replaced before departure.

column1: The flight departed into known thunderstorms along the SID
column2: after a weather deviation the company later questioned the dispatch release.

column1: An incorrect altimeter setting from ATIS caused a 300-ft high approach
column2: the error was corrected after a low-altitude alert from ATC.

column1: The cabin door seal leaked during climb
column2: pressurization was maintained and maintenance resealed the door at destination.

column1: A rejected takeoff was initiated for an engine oil-filter bypass light at 80 kt
column2: the aircraft taxied clear and maintenance inspected the engine.

column1: FOQA data later showed an unstable approach that the crew believed was stable
column2: training emphasized the stabilized-approach gate.

column1: A temporary flight restriction for VIP movement was not in the preflight package
column2: ATC turned the flight away from the restricted area.

column1: The crew smelled electrical smoke after selecting the windshield heat
column2: the switch was turned off and the odor dissipated.

column1: During single-engine taxi training the aircraft stopped short of the hold-short line after a radio blocked clearance readback.
A cargo net was found unsecured after departure on a prior sector's report
column2: the next crew re-secured all nets before pushback.

column1: The captain cancelled IFR for a visual approach into rising terrain at night
column2: the FO successfully challenged and IFR was retained.

column1: An airspeed disagreement between PFDs appeared in IMC
column2: the crew flew the reliable side per memory items and diverted.

column1: Deice fluid residue on the windshield reduced visibility on takeoff roll
column2: the takeoff was rejected below 60 kt.

column1: A maintenance error left a pitot cover installed
column2: the cover was noticed during walkaround by the FO.

column1: The crew received a low-fuel advisory after an unexpectedly long hold
column2: they declared minimum fuel and received priority handling.

column1: An aft cargo door open indication after takeoff led to an air turnback
column2: the door was found closed but the proximity sensor failed.

column1: During a CAT II approach the autoland disconnect light illuminated at 200 ft
column2: a missed approach was flown.

column1: A jumpseat qualified mechanic riding along identified an unusual vibration the crew had normalized
column2: the aircraft was grounded for inspection.

column1: ATC issued a land-and-hold-short clearance the crew could not accept due to landing distance
column2: they requested full length.

column1: The FO's EFB failed during the approach briefing
column2: paper charts were used and the approach continued.

column1: A fuel imbalance checklist was started in error after a gauge fluctuation
column2: crossfeed was never opened and quantity later stabilized.

column1: Cabin pressure climbed abnormally fast after takeoff
column2: the outflow valve was manually controlled and the flight leveled at a lower altitude.

column1: A contract fueler pumped Jet-A into an aircraft that had ordered a lesser uplift
column2: the discrepancy was caught on the fuel slip before push.

column1: The crew reported laser illumination on short final
column2: ATC advised law enforcement and the approach was continued to landing.

column1: An MEL placard for an inoperative pack was missing from the cockpit
column2: the FO refused dispatch until the placard was installed.

column1: Wake encounter on a closely spaced parallel approach caused a momentary stick-shaker
column2: the crew went around.

column1: A battery temperature rise after APU start led to APU shutdown and GPU use for the remainder of the turn.
The flight released with thunderstorms forecast at ETA
column2: holding fuel was inadequate after two weather deviations and the flight diverted.

column1: A nose gear tire was found worn to cord during preflight
column2: the tire was changed and the departure delayed.

column1: During climb the cabin climbed through 10,000 ft before the warning; the crew donned masks and initiated an emergency descent.
An incorrect runway was loaded for performance calculation
column2: actual runway was shorter and takeoff was delayed for recalculation.

column1: The FO called for flaps 15 when the procedure called for flaps 5
column2: the PF caught the error before configuration change.

column1: A cargo smoke detector false-alarm history was not briefed
column2: when the warning returned the crew treated it as real and diverted.

column1: Ground personnel walked under an engine with the beacon on
column2: the captain shut down and held a safety briefing before restart.

column1: The aircraft's GPS lost RAIM during an RNAV approach
column2: the crew broke off and flew a VOR approach instead.

column1: A recurring write-up for yaw damper disconnects continued after three logbook closures
column2: engineering issued a fleet alert.

column1: On a ferry flight the crew exceeded a flap speed limitation by 10 kt
column2: the exceedance was entered in the logbook for inspection.
